argument: Measured in source, deleting the named tables is not a structure-neutral edit: the chapter files keep their headings and lose the content under them, so the purge as drafted leaves three render defects and one misattribution. Chapter 16 in 123 lines carries seven explicit page breaks, and the armour table is bracketed exactly by the breaks at lines 29 and 54 with one sentence below it, so removing the table produces a forced full page holding a section heading and a single line of prose. In chapter 15 the Armor section is 26 lines of which 17 are its table; what survives is four non-empty lines, two of them forwarding crossref stubs that point at chapter 16 rather than stating anything. Adventuring Gear is 58 lines of which 47 are its table; what survives is six non-empty lines and no subsection to absorb the freed space, so the heading outlives the gear it names. Neither stub section owns a subsection, so the page mass cannot redistribute downward. The Weapons section does keep substance, but its seven property bullets convey each property's scope only through parenthetical lists of table rows, so eight residual lines index labels that will no longer exist. Against that, the width and break-header surfaces are clean and must not be blamed: all eleven tables in the two chapters sum their column percentages to exactly 100.00, and every table already declares a repeating header row, so no new overflow or split-header defect is introduced by row removal. The repair is therefore structural, not typographic: restate the property bullets to carry scope without naming rows, fold or re-content the two stub sections, delete the ch16 break pair at 29 and 54 with the table, and re-place the chapter 15 breaks at 17, 221 and 264. One further render fact: the chapter 15 Armor table is the only one of the ten tables there missing the unnumbered setting, so it presently renders with an auto caption the other nine lack; that defect is retired by the table's removal. Caveat: these are source-level measurements, and the actual rendered page count after purge should be confirmed on a clean build.

evidence.claim: The five named tables in chapter 15 account for just under a third of the chapter's lines and a third of its bytes, so the freed page mass is large and must be redistributed deliberately.
